title: What enforcement documents say about these routes
question: What have the Controller, the Ethics Commission and the Budget and Legislative Analyst put in writing about gifts to departments, commissioners' interests, measure committees, public campaign money and enforcement?
finding: 16 passages from 14 documents dated 2019 to 2026: the Controller on money raised for departments outside City books and on support organizations' record-keeping; settled cases on a friends-of gift, a commissioner's votes and a measure committee that paid a candidate's campaign; the Ethics Commission on audits of publicly financed campaigns it could not complete; and the yearly counts of non-filers and whistleblower reports.
how: Each row is one document in the project's library of official documents, with a quotation of at most twelve words and a one-sentence summary. The script checks every quotation, and every figure in the summaries taken from a document, against the document's text and stops if one is missing; penalty amounts come from the Ethics Commission's penalty file.
limits: These are the documents on file, chosen because they bear on the five routes; they are not everything written on the subject, and a settlement records what a respondent admitted, not a court's finding. Signed stipulations that are scanned images cannot be quoted and are left out, including one 2026 settlement with a member of the Board of Supervisors. The Controller's 2020 review was labelled preliminary, and the joint review of the Parks Alliance announced in 2025 has not been published.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller's Office (City Services Auditor)
rows.document: Public Integrity Review preliminary assessment: Gifts to departments through non-City organizations
rows.quote: “were not accepted or disclosed by the City”
rows.said: The Controller found that the Public Works director asked firms with City contracts or building permits for money that was held in accounts at the Parks Alliance and spent outside City purchasing rules; 33 departments reported non-City organizations with 588 accounts.

rows.document: Stipulation, decision and order - Deborah Raphael (Case 21-22-000359)
rows.quote: “an unincorporated nonprofit entity created to support the Department”
rows.said: The Environment director admitted taking a gift in 2018 from her department's own friends-of organization and signing a grant agreement with it the same year; the penalty was $4,000.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller's Office (City Services Auditor)
rows.document: Support Organizations Must Better Comply With City Agreements to Improve Public Trust and Accountability
rows.quote: “did not ensure that Parks Alliance maintained sufficient documentation”
rows.said: The Controller's audit found Recreation and Park had not ensured the Parks Alliance kept documentation for $848,670 (50%) of $1,700,038 in payments sampled.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller's Office (City Services Auditor)
rows.document: Support Organizations Must Better Comply With City Agreements to Improve Public Trust and Accountability
rows.quote: “lacked written processes to ensure compliance with their MOU’s conflict-of-interest requirements”
rows.said: The same audit found support organizations did not meet some disclosure requirements of their agreements, including posting financial reports and funding sources, and had no written conflict-of-interest process, though no conflict was found.

rows.document: Performance Audit of Citywide Management of Conflicts of Interest (Budget and Legislative Analyst; posted with the Ethics Commission's meeting papers)
rows.quote: “no citywide process or documented assurance that these reviews are being completed”
rows.said: The Budget and Legislative Analyst found no citywide assurance that departments review the Form 700s of about 4,500 filers, and conflict-of-interest forms on file for only 21 of 66 contracts sampled (32%).

rows.document: List of Officers & Employees Without 2025 Annual Filings
rows.quote: “may not participate in nor vote at meetings until they have filed”
rows.said: The Ethics Commission's list of June 2, 2025 named board members and commissioners who had not filed the statement due April 1; 6 entries on it were missing a Form 700.

rows.document: Stipulation, decision and order - Sophia Andary (Case 25-001001)
rows.quote: “voted to approve the waiver request unanimously”
rows.said: A Commissioner on the Status of Women voted for a sole-source grant of $500,000, later $700,000, to an organization that then sent her a $1,000 honorarium; the penalty was $1,000.

rows.document: December 12, 2025 – Agenda Item 5: Quarterly Enforcement Report
rows.quote: “there are 79 filers (1.3%) who failed to file”
rows.said: Of 5,958 people due to file a Form 700 in 2025, 337 filed late and 79 had not filed by December; the Commission opened cases on 21 of 234 people still out of compliance after a grace period.

rows.document: Stipulation, decision and order - Kathrin Moore (Case 26-001012)
rows.quote: “voted four separate times on three separate projects”
rows.said: A Planning Commissioner admitted voting on three projects whose architect had paid her about $60,000 in retirement income during the period; the penalty was $12,000.

rows.document: Ethics Commission Fines Political Committee Progress San Francisco $29,300 for Failing To Accurately Report $1.1 Million in Campaign Contributions
rows.quote: “Failing To Accurately Report $1.1 Million in Campaign Contributions”
rows.said: A general-purpose committee, its principal officer and its treasurer were fined $29,300 on twenty-five counts for reporting failures over three elections from June 2018.

rows.document: Ethics Commission Issues Record $108,179.99 Penalty to Mark Farrell’s Committees for Making and Accepting Prohibited Contributions
rows.quote: “The penalty is the largest in the history of the Ethics Commission.”
rows.said: The ballot-measure committee named for a candidate for Mayor paid his campaign committee nearly $100,000 for which it received nothing in return; the committees, the candidate and the treasurer were fined $108,180.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.quote: “public funds are currently distributed to candidates in three tiers”
rows.said: The Budget and Legislative Analyst described the matching programme as it stood in 2019: three tiers with different match rates, the first matching $100 of each contribution.

rows.quote: “unable to complete mandatory audits of publicly financed candidates”
rows.said: The Ethics Commission approved $8.8 million of public funds for 27 candidates in November 2024 and reported that it had not completed the required audits for the 2020 and 2022 elections.

rows.document: September 11, 2026 – Agenda Item 4: Executive Director’s Report
rows.said: The Commission's director reported that all 27 audits of publicly financed 2024 campaigns were completed about a year after the election.

rows.quote: “imposed no administrative penalties in whistleblower retaliation cases”
rows.said: The Ethics Commission resolved 23 whistleblower-retaliation matters in fiscal 2025, 11 dismissed on first review and 12 closed after investigation, with no violation found and no penalty.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller's Office (City Services Auditor)
rows.document: Whistleblower Program Annual Report and Quarter 4 Results, Fiscal Year 2025-26
rows.said: The Controller's whistleblower programme closed 422 investigations in fiscal 2026; 115 (27%) led a department or contractor to take 124 corrective or preventive actions.
